entry.title: Wave-Based Dispatch for Circuit Cutting in Hybrid HPC--Quantum Systems
entry.summary: Hybrid HPC-quantum workloads based on circuit cutting decompose large quantum circuits into independent fragments, but existing frameworks tightly couple cutting logic to execution orchestration, preventing HPC centers from applying mature resource management policies to NISQ workloads. We present DQR (Dynamic Queue Router), a runtime framework that treats circuit fragments as first-class schedulable units. DQR introduces a backend-agnostic fragment descriptor, a wave-based coordinator enabling pipeline concurrency through non-blocking polling, and a production-ready implementation on the CESGA Qmio supercomputer integrating local and cloud quantum backends. Experiments on a 32-qubit Hardware-Efficient Ansatz demonstrate makespan improvements over a monolithic CPU baseline together with transparent per-fragment failover recovery without pipeline restart.
